sections.html: Moniteau is a rural county in central Missouri with about 15,400 residents. California is the seat and largest city, and the county belongs to the Jefferson City metro area. There are 5,729 households averaging 2.45 people, and roughly four in five homes are lived in by their owners. Owners put the median home value at $181,900, and median rent is $735. Only 6 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction is thin and resale houses make up most of the market. Other communities include Clarksburg, Jamestown, Lupus and Tipton, plus Fortuna and Latham, and six school districts serve the county.

sections.h2: Which Moniteau County offices handle your tax bill?
sections.html:
Everything runs through the courthouse at 200 E. Main Street in California. Both offices below keep weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30 and close on holidays.

  • Assessor, Room 105. Call 573-796-4637 or write assessor@moniteaucountymo.gov. This office sets the value of every piece of taxable real and personal property in the county.
  • Collector, Room 101. Call 573-796-4521. The collector prints the statements, passes the money on to schools and other taxing districts each month, issues merchant licenses and holds the August sale of delinquent land. Staff work through the noon hour.
  • Recorder, Room 102. The circuit clerk also serves as recorder, at 573-796-2071.

When a statement arrives, check the address, the listed vehicles and the legal description. You can pay at the counter, by phone, by mail or on the collector's website, using cash, a personal check, an e-check, a money order or a credit card.

Real estate is revalued every other year. Section 137.115 fixes new assessed values as of January 1 of an odd-numbered year, and they carry through the next even-numbered year, with new construction the exception.

Missouri taxes only a slice of market value, and the slice depends on the subclass. Subclass 1 real property is assessed at 19 percent, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent. Personal property is assessed at 33 and one third percent, with lower rates for livestock, farm machinery, poultry and a few other items. Ask the assessor how your parcel is classified. A manufactured home used as a dwelling gets the residential percentage.

Before an assessor raises a subclass 1 value by more than fifteen percent, excluding new construction, someone must inspect the property on site. A drive-by does not count. You can ask that the inspection include the interior, and you have at least thirty days after written notice to make that request.

The tax year starts January 1, the valuation date, and payment closes December 31. Personal property lists go to the assessor, and late fees begin if a list comes back after March 1. Anyone living in the county on January 1 should list cars, boats and equipment, and a mobile home on someone else's land goes on the list too. Household goods, inventories, clothing and items of personal use are exempt.

Moniteau County dates to remember
WhenWhat happens
January 1Values are fixed for the year
March 1Personal property list is due, or late fees accrue
Second Monday of JulyLast day to file with the local equalization board
Early NovemberBills are mailed
After December 31Unpaid bills are delinquent
Fourth Monday of AugustDelinquent land can be sold

If November ends and no bill has shown up, call the collector right away. A missing bill does not cancel the tax, the penalty or the interest. A divorcing couple should also know that the collector cannot split a statement after it is issued.

There are three steps. Talk to the assessor, then take the dispute to the county equalization board, and last to the State Tax Commission. The board filing deadline is the second Monday of July. After the board mails its decision, the next appeal is due thirty days from the date of that letter, a rule section 138.430 backs with its "whichever date later occurs" wording.

Some owners can skip the board and file directly with the commission in two cases:

  • The assessor never told the current owner about a new or higher value at least thirty days before the board deadline.
  • A new owner closed on a purchase less than thirty days after the county mailed the tax statement.

Property titled to a corporation, LLC, limited partnership, trust or estate must be appealed through an attorney.

A dispute does not pause the due date. To avoid interest, send the full amount to the collector by December 31, write "paid under protest" on the check, and attach a written statement of your reasons and the value you think is fair. Pay without a protest and without an appeal, and that year's assessment is closed to challenge, though next year's stays open.

The Property Tax Credit Claim draws the most questions. It is a credit for certain seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals, worth up to $1,100 for homeowners who live in the house and up to $750 for renters. The amount turns on what you paid in tax or rent and on total household income, taxable and not.

A former prisoner of war with a total service-connected disability has a constitutional exemption on the homestead they own and occupy. To claim it, give the assessor proof of residence, a federal letter confirming the disability and either a DD 214 or an archives or VA letter establishing POW status.

Service members away on military orders owe no interest on late payment, though a collection fee may still apply. Confirm current rules with the assessor or collector before you plan around any program.

Ask the collector what the parcel owes today, penalty and interest included, before you sign any contract. Under section 140.150, land with unpaid tax is subject to the August sale on the fourth Monday. The owner can still clear the taxes, penalty, interest and costs at the collector's office until the sale happens. The collector must first mail notice to the recorded owner, and a certified second notice follows when assessed value tops $1,000.

Have whoever handles your closing settle the balance with the collector's office so nothing stays attached to the parcel. A cash buyer can close with the tax payoff taken from your proceeds, which avoids waiting on a lender to approve a parcel with an open balance. Our Missouri property tax guide explains how appeals work statewide, and the Missouri homestead page covers exemptions. The collector's website carries the current levy sheet for anyone estimating a bill.

faqs.q: Which office sends property tax statements in Moniteau County?
faqs.a: The collector in Room 101 at the California courthouse prints and mails them each November. The assessor in Room 105 supplies the values behind them.

faqs.q: What day do unpaid Moniteau County taxes turn delinquent?
faqs.a: Anything still owed after December 31. The collector then offers the land at the August sale, and the owner may still pay before the sale.

faqs.q: By when must I contest a value?
faqs.a: The county board's filing deadline is the second Monday of July. After the board's letter, you have thirty days to continue to the State Tax Commission.

faqs.q: What share of my house's worth is taxed?
faqs.a: Subclass 1 real property is assessed at 19 percent of true value, subclass 2 at 12 percent and subclass 3 at 32 percent. Your assessor can name the class for your parcel.

faqs.q: Is there a credit for older homeowners?
faqs.a: Seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals may file Missouri's Property Tax Credit Claim, which pays up to $1,100 to homeowners who occupy their house. Income and the tax actually paid set the amount.
